A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same joint-recall and HAX research. All 18 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original joint-recall experiments, continual-pretraining curves, RULER and LongBench evaluations, and appendix short-context results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results, replaces the downstream benchmark evaluations, and adds explicit doubled-width baseline results and a 4K context extrapolation evaluation.

M1.justification: The LSH and key-selection procedures, scoring network, ranking loss, combined objective, and HAX integration remain unchanged in Section 4. The redesigned architecture illustration does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Downstream continual pretraining switches from The Pile to TxT360, while the Pile experiment remains for Figure 4. Appendix E.1 adds a 4K extrapolation scenario, including RULER QA2. Coverage otherwise retains the same recall, language-modeling, LongBench English, and short-context task families.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Mamba/Mamba2, Samba, and the D, SW, SW+D, A, LSH, and KS variants. Table 3 separately reports doubled-width base models already described in v1; this concerns model-size controls and result reporting rather than a new comparison method.

E3.justification: The stated downstream setup changes from 130M models with 10K continual-pretraining and 3K instruction-tuning steps to 790M models with 50K and 10K steps. Pretraining context changes from 3,072 to 2,048 tokens; Appendix D.2 revises filtering and learning-rate/warm-up schedules. Joint-recall sample counts change from 1M/10K/10K to 1.4M/14.4K/14.4K. The new extrapolation protocol tests 2K-trained models at 4K.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.1 directly tests context-length extrapolation from 2K training to 4K evaluation. The component ablations, short-context retention analysis, and Figure 9 attention-pattern case study were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Joint recall still uses three random seeds per learning rate and reports the average for the best-performing learning rate. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures accompany the revised downstream results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 report replacement results under changed settings: Mamba/HAX RULER averages are 26.7/32.9 in v1 and 42.43/44.57 in v2; LongBench averages are 11.10/11.34 and 19.79/19.95. These are not same-setting gains. Table 3 adds doubled-width scores of 34.5 and 59.2, and Section 5.1 drops the greater-than-100% improvement statement. New 4K results give HAX 28.20 versus Mamba 27.04. Figure 4 and the short-context scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Corollary 3.1, Propositions 3.2–3.3, binning equivalence in Appendix A, proofs in Appendix B, and multilevel formulation and proof in Appendix C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: joint recall captures context-dependent retrieval, CDSA overcomes the stated expressiveness limitation, and HAX outperforms SSM and CISA baselines.

C2.justification: Appendix E.1 newly interprets the 4K results as evidence of robustness to context-length extrapolation. Existing explanations of LSH/KS complementarity, training stability, and short-context retention remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly reports approximately 1% parameter overhead and distinguishes the 130M/Pile curve from the 790M/TxT360 downstream experiments. Appendix D revises the documented training recipe but removes explicit zero initialization of the gate and lowest-validation-loss checkpoint selection. Those omissions do not establish procedural changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds the TxT360 citation by Tang et al. (2024). The related-work discussion and positioning relative to SSMs, sparse attention, and hybrid architectures otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites in Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix D reorganize the experimental descriptions. Appendix E inserts an extrapolation subsection and renumbers the short-context subsection. The broader narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 replaces the generic integration and Mamba/Mamba2 schematics with LSH/KS attention-pattern illustrations and a Mamba diagram, removing the Mamba2 panel and legend. Table 3 gains a width-control row, a new 4K Table 4 is inserted, and the retained short-context table becomes Table 5. Other changes are localized reflow and resizing.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens empirical support through explicit doubled-width controls and direct 2K-to-4K extrapolation evidence, while distinguishing the larger-model downstream setup more clearly. These help assess capacity confounds and applicability. The higher replacement scores do not establish comparable performance gains, and removal of gate-initialization and checkpoint-selection details limits the reproducibility benefit.
